title: Codex thread created by a timed-out thread/start can never be suppressed (id never learned)
outcome:
Second half of the duplicate-session leak, NOT fixed by the in-flight guard in tm-7rm.

Orphan suppression (codex.rs suppress_orphaned_new_thread) only runs on the waiter's Ok path — it needs the thread id out of the thread/start RESPONSE. When the app-server times out (SHARED_CODEX_THREAD_SETUP_TIMEOUT = 180s) or the runtime is torn down, the Err path (handle_shared_codex_thread_setup_response_error_if_current) fails the turn but has NO thread id to suppress — while the Codex app-server has ALREADY written the thread to disk.

Result: every failed thread setup leaves exactly one orphan thread that discovery later imports as a phantom top-level 'Ready to continue this Codex thread' session, and it can never be suppressed because TermAl never learned its id.

Measured: of 8 threads from one delegation, 6 were neither bound nor suppressed. The tm-7rm guard reduces this to at most 1 orphan per failed setup instead of N, but does not eliminate it.

Trigger is the Codex app-server flakiness tracked in tm-ztk.

Fix directions: (a) reconcile after a failed setup — a thread created in the failure window for our cwd with no owning session can be suppressed or adopted; (b) ask the Codex app-server for a client-supplied thread id / idempotency key so a retried setup cannot mint a second thread; (c) at minimum, log it so the leak is visible.
